title: Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue — Travel Protection Plans
content:
Cover under the Travel Protection Plans may be given up in the period immediately after the certificate is
issued, on the conditions set out here as clauses of the certificate wording.

## Who may give up cover

Only the policyholder may give up their own cover, and the cancellation is confirmed by the policyholder rather
than performed on their behalf.

## The free-look period

The free-look period is counted in whole calendar days from the day after the issue date, weekends and public
holidays included, and a cancellation confirmed exactly on the closing day is still inside the period. The
period runs from the moment the certificate of insurance was issued to the policyholder, which is the moment the
policy record itself carries and not the moment the traveller says they read the certificate; its length is the
free-look period of the plan held.

The clause "A free-look cancellation is handled at the full refund only when frozen time is not after the moment
the certificate of insurance was issued to the policyholder plus the free-look period of the plan held." is
**no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which the share of premium returned is
fixed when a policyholder gives up their own cover.

## The terms that stand

1. Inside the free-look period the whole premium is returned to the original form of payment, the policy fee
   excepted, and the agency's commission is recovered in full.
2. The free-look right is lost as soon as the journey has begun or a claim has been filed, whichever comes
   first, however many days of the period remain.
3. Outside the free-look period the mid-term terms apply instead, and the two are never combined.

The clause "A returned premium is raised against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy
with several premium lines returns as several refund lines." is **no longer in force**, having been
superseded by the current basis on which the line a returned premium is raised against is settled.

## Counting the period

| Where the plan's free-look period is 14 days and the certificate was issued on the 3rd | The period |
|---|---|
| The count begins | On the 4th, the day after the issue date |
| The closing day | The 17th, weekends and public holidays counted as days |
| A cancellation confirmed on the 17th | Inside the period |
| A cancellation confirmed on the 18th | Outside the period, and the mid-term terms apply instead |

The dates in that illustration are hypothetical. Note that on the 12th of the same illustration, with two days
of the period still to run, a traveller who has already begun the journey or already filed a claim has lost the
free-look right notwithstanding.

superseded_clauses: A free-look cancellation is handled at the full refund only when frozen time is not after the moment the certificate of insurance was issued to the policyholder plus the free-look period of the plan held.
A returned premium is raised against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as several refund lines.
